title: How to Write a Wedding Invitation Message for WhatsApp: 20 Examples for Nigerian Couples
excerpt: Looking for a wedding invitation message for WhatsApp? Find 20 formal, simple and friendly examples for Nigerian weddings, plus tips for inviting guests.
author: Ariya Journal
imageAlt: Black woman using a smartphone to view wedding invitation details
content:
Introduction

Planning a wedding in Nigeria involves bringing together family members, friends, colleagues, neighbours and other important people in your life. Once the wedding date and venue have been confirmed, one of the next important tasks is inviting your guests.

While printed wedding invitation cards remain important for many Nigerian couples, WhatsApp has become a convenient way to share wedding invitations, especially with friends, colleagues, younger relatives and guests who live in different cities or countries.

However, sending a wedding invitation through WhatsApp is not simply about forwarding a picture of your invitation card. The accompanying message matters too. It should make the recipient feel personally invited, communicate the important details and explain what they need to do next.

If you are wondering what to write when sending a wedding invitation on WhatsApp, this guide provides 20 examples you can adapt for different people and wedding ceremonies.

Whether you are inviting an elderly relative, sending a formal invitation on behalf of your parents, or sharing your wedding details with close friends, you will find a suitable message below.

What Should a Wedding Invitation Message for WhatsApp Include?

A good WhatsApp wedding invitation message should be brief, respectful and clear. You do not need to repeat every detail already displayed on your invitation card, but the recipient should understand what the message is about without having to guess.

Before sending your message, make sure it contains the following information where relevant:

1. A personal greeting

Start with a greeting that suits your relationship with the recipient.

For example:

  • Dear Uncle [Name]
  • Good afternoon, Aunty [Name]
  • Hello [Name]
  • Dear Mr and Mrs [Surname]
  • Good evening, Ma

For close friends, a more relaxed greeting may be appropriate.

2. The names of the couple

Clearly identify who is getting married. Do not assume that every recipient will immediately recognise the names on a forwarded invitation.

3. The wedding date

Include the day and date of the wedding. Writing the date in full can help prevent confusion.

For example: Saturday, 12 December 2026.

4. The venue or location

Mention the city or main venue, even if the full address is on the invitation card.

This is particularly helpful when guests are travelling from another state or need to make arrangements ahead of the wedding.

5. The invitation card or website link

Attach the digital invitation, a clear picture of the invitation card or a link to the wedding information page.

If you have a wedding website, it can provide guests with additional information such as the event schedule, venue directions, accommodation guidance and other relevant details.

6. RSVP instructions, if required

If you need guests to confirm attendance, include a clear deadline and tell them how to respond.

For example:

"Kindly confirm your attendance by 25 November 2026 using the RSVP link below."

Do not include an RSVP instruction unless you have a process for receiving and managing responses.

20 Wedding Invitation Messages for WhatsApp

The following examples are written for different Nigerian wedding situations. Replace the details in brackets with your own information before sending.

1. Simple wedding invitation message

Use this when you want a short message that works for most guests.

Hello [Guest Name],

We are delighted to invite you to celebrate the wedding of [Bride's Name] and [Groom's Name] on [Day, Date] at [Venue], [City].

It would mean so much to have you celebrate this special occasion with us.

Please find our invitation below.

[Attach Invitation]

With love, [Couple's Names]

2. Formal wedding invitation message

This version is suitable for senior relatives, family friends, respected members of the community and people you do not communicate with casually.

Dear [Title and Name],

With great joy and gratitude, we cordially invite you to the wedding celebration of [Bride's Name] and [Groom's Name], taking place on [Day, Date] at [Venue], [City].

We would be honoured by your presence as we celebrate this important milestone.

Kindly find the invitation and event details attached.

We look forward to celebrating with you.

Warm regards, [Couple's Names]

3. Wedding invitation message from the couple

This is appropriate when the bride and groom are personally sending the invitation.

Hello [Guest Name],

We are excited to share that we are getting married!

We would love for you to join us as we celebrate our union on [Day, Date] at [Venue], [City].

Your presence would make our day even more special.

Please see our invitation for the full details.

[Invitation Link or Attachment]

With love, [Bride's Name] and [Groom's Name]

4. Wedding invitation message from parents

In many Nigerian families, parents and families play an important role in inviting guests to a wedding. This version is suitable when the invitation is being sent on behalf of the couple's parents.

Dear [Guest Name],

With hearts full of joy and gratitude to God, the families of [Bride's Family Name] and [Groom's Family Name] are delighted to invite you to the wedding ceremony of their children, [Bride's Name] and [Groom's Name].

The celebration will take place on [Day, Date] at [Venue], [City].

We would be delighted to have you share in this memorable occasion with our families.

Kindly find the invitation attached.

Warm regards, [Parents' Names or Family Name]

5. Wedding invitation message for close friends

A wedding invitation to a close friend can be warm and conversational without losing the important details.

Hey [Friend's Name]!

The big day is finally here! I'm getting married to [Partner's Name], and I really want you to be part of the celebration.

Our wedding is happening on [Day, Date] at [Venue], [City].

I would love to celebrate this special moment with you.

Here's the invitation: [Invitation Link or Attachment]

Hope to see you there!

6. Wedding invitation message for colleagues

Use a courteous and professional tone when inviting colleagues, business associates or professional contacts.

Good afternoon, [Name].

I am pleased to invite you to celebrate my wedding with [Partner's Name] on [Day, Date] at [Venue], [City].

It would be a pleasure to have you join us on this special occasion.

Please find the invitation attached for further details.

Thank you, and I hope you can celebrate with us.

Best regards, [Your Name]

7. Traditional wedding invitation message

Traditional weddings often involve family participation and cultural customs. Your invitation should identify the ceremony clearly and use the appropriate family names and titles.

Dear [Guest Name],

With joy and gratitude, our families warmly invite you to the traditional marriage ceremony of [Bride's Name] and [Groom's Name].

The ceremony will take place on [Day, Date] at [Venue], [City], beginning at [Time].

We would be honoured to have you join our families as we celebrate this beautiful union.

Kindly find the invitation attached.

Warm regards, [Family Names]

8. White wedding invitation message

Dear [Guest Name],

We are delighted to invite you to witness and celebrate the white wedding ceremony of [Bride's Name] and [Groom's Name].

The ceremony will hold on [Day, Date] at [Church or Venue], [City], by [Time].

A reception will follow at [Reception Venue].

Your presence and good wishes would mean a great deal to us.

Please see the attached invitation for further details.

With love, [Couple's Names]

9. Combined traditional and white wedding invitation

If you are organising both ceremonies, make sure the recipient understands the dates, venues and times for each event.

Dear [Guest Name],

With the blessings of our families, we are delighted to invite you to celebrate our wedding.

Our traditional wedding will take place on [Day, Date] at [Venue], [City].

Our white wedding will follow on [Day, Date] at [Church or Venue], with the reception holding at [Reception Venue].

We would be honoured to have you celebrate these special moments with us.

Kindly find the full invitation and event details attached.

With love, [Bride's Name] and [Groom's Name]

10. Short wedding invitation message

This is useful when you are sending a wedding invitation card and only need a brief accompanying message.

Hello [Guest Name],

You are warmly invited to the wedding of [Bride's Name] and [Groom's Name] on [Day, Date].

We would love to celebrate with you!

Please see the attached invitation for the full details.

[Couple's Names]

11. Wedding invitation message for elderly relatives

When inviting elderly relatives, consider using a respectful greeting and a warm expression of appreciation.

Good afternoon, Aunty/Uncle [Name].

With great joy, we would like to invite you to the wedding of [Bride's Name] and [Groom's Name] on [Day, Date] at [Venue], [City].

Your presence, prayers and blessings would mean so much to us as we begin this new chapter.

Kindly find the invitation attached.

We sincerely hope you can join us.

Warm regards, [Couple's Names]

12. Religious wedding invitation message

Choose the greeting and wording that reflect the couple's faith and the recipient's preferences.

Christian wedding example

Greetings in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

With gratitude to God, we are pleased to invite you to the wedding of [Bride's Name] and [Groom's Name] on [Day, Date] at [Venue].

We would be delighted to have you join us in celebrating this special day and sharing in our joy.

Please find our invitation attached.

God bless you, [Couple's Names]

Muslim wedding example

Assalamu Alaikum.

With gratitude to Allah, we warmly invite you to the wedding celebration of [Bride's Name] and [Groom's Name] on [Day, Date] at [Venue], [City].

We would be honoured by your presence and prayers as we celebrate this special occasion.

Kindly find the invitation attached.

Jazakumullahu Khairan, [Couple's Names]

13. Wedding invitation message for guests travelling from another city

Some guests may need to arrange transport, accommodation or time away from work. Send this message early enough for them to plan.

Hello [Guest Name],

We are excited to invite you to our wedding celebration on [Day, Date] in [City].

We understand that you may need to make travel arrangements, so we wanted to share the details with you ahead of time.

Our invitation and event information are available below:

[Invitation Link]

It would mean a lot to have you celebrate with us.

With love, [Couple's Names]

14. Wedding invitation message for family groups

Use this when the entire WhatsApp group consists of people you intend to invite.

Hello everyone!

We are delighted to announce that [Bride's Name] and [Groom's Name] are getting married!

We warmly invite you all to celebrate with us on [Day, Date] at [Venue], [City].

Your love, support and presence would make the occasion even more special.

Please find the invitation and event details attached.

We look forward to celebrating with you!

Important: Only use a group invitation when everyone in the group is actually invited. If the invitation applies to particular family members or households, send it privately to avoid misunderstandings.

15. Wedding invitation message with an RSVP request

If you need to confirm attendance before the wedding, make the next step clear.

Dear [Guest Name],

We are delighted to invite you to the wedding of [Bride's Name] and [Groom's Name] on [Day, Date] at [Venue], [City].

We would love to have you celebrate with us.

Kindly confirm whether you will be attending by [RSVP Deadline] using the link below:

[RSVP Link]

Thank you, and we look forward to celebrating with you!

16. Wedding invitation message with a location link

This is useful when guests may be unfamiliar with the venue or travelling through a busy city.

Hello [Guest Name],

We would love to have you join us for the wedding of [Bride's Name] and [Groom's Name] on [Day, Date] at [Venue], [City].

Here is our invitation with the event details:

[Invitation Link]

You can also use the location link below to find the venue:

[Google Maps Location Link]

We look forward to seeing you!

17. Wedding invitation message for a destination or out-of-town wedding

Dear [Guest Name],

We are excited to invite you to celebrate our wedding on [Day, Date] in [City or Destination].

We know attending may require some planning, so we have included the event schedule and relevant information in our invitation.

Please find everything here:

[Wedding Website or Invitation Link]

It would mean so much to have you with us.

With love, [Couple's Names]

18. Wedding invitation message for a second reminder

Use this when you have already sent the invitation and want to remind guests about the approaching date.

Hello [Guest Name],

We hope you are doing well.

This is a gentle reminder about the wedding of [Bride's Name] and [Groom's Name,] taking place on [Day, Date] at [Venue].

We would be delighted to have you celebrate with us.

For the full details, kindly revisit the invitation below:

[Invitation Link]

We look forward to seeing you!

19. Wedding invitation message for guests who have not responded

A follow-up should be polite and should not make the recipient feel pressured.

Hello [Guest Name],

We hope you are doing well.

We are following up on the wedding invitation we shared earlier for [Bride's Name] and [Groom's Name].

Kindly let us know if you will be able to attend by [RSVP Deadline] so we can finalise our arrangements.

You can confirm here:

[RSVP Link]

Thank you, and we hope to celebrate with you!

20. Wedding invitation message for a very intimate wedding

If you are having a small wedding, the message can communicate the personal nature of the celebration.

Hello [Guest Name],

We are having a small and intimate wedding celebration, and it would mean so much to have you there with us.

Please join us as [Bride's Name] and [Groom's Name] celebrate their wedding on [Day, Date] at [Venue].

We would be delighted to share this special moment with you.

Please find your invitation below.

With love, [Couple's Names]

How to Send a Wedding Invitation on WhatsApp Properly

Having the right wording is only one part of the process. How you send the invitation can influence whether guests notice it, understand it and respond.

Here are practical steps to follow.

1. Prepare the invitation before sending the message

Before opening WhatsApp, make sure your invitation is complete.

Check that it includes:

  • The correct names of the couple.
  • The wedding date and time.
  • The ceremony venue.
  • The reception venue, if different.
  • Relevant dress code or colour information.
  • RSVP details, if applicable.
  • Any important instructions guests need to know.

Ask someone else to proofread the invitation before sending it.

2. Personalise the message

Avoid sending the same impersonal message to everyone if you can make it more personal.

For example, a message to an elderly family member should not necessarily sound like one sent to a close university friend.

A short greeting with the person's name can make the invitation feel more thoughtful.

3. Attach the invitation or share the correct link

You can send your invitation as an image, PDF or link, depending on how it was created.

If you use a wedding website, make sure the link opens correctly and that the information is accessible to the intended guests.

4. Include the venue location

Nigerian weddings may attract guests travelling across different parts of a city or from other states.

Where possible, include a Google Maps location link or clear directions to the venue.

Do not assume that every guest knows the location simply because the venue name is familiar.

5. Send invitations individually where appropriate

Personal messages are often more suitable for close relatives, senior guests and people receiving invitations with specific guest allocations.

WhatsApp broadcast lists may also be useful, but remember that recipients' privacy and WhatsApp's contact and delivery requirements matter.

Avoid adding people to a group simply to announce a wedding if they have not been invited.

6. Give guests enough time to respond

If you require an RSVP, state the deadline clearly.

Allow enough time to finalise catering, seating, venue arrangements and other wedding logistics.

7. Follow up politely

Some guests may see the invitation and forget to respond.

A short, respectful reminder can help you confirm attendance without making anyone feel uncomfortable.

Common Mistakes to Avoid When Sending Wedding Invitations on WhatsApp

Even a beautifully designed invitation can create confusion if the accompanying message is unclear.

Avoid these mistakes:

1. Sending an invitation without identifying the couple. Always mention the names of the people getting married.

2. Leaving out the wedding date. Make sure the date is easy to find, even if the invitation contains it.

3. Using an unclear venue description. Include the city and, where appropriate, a location link.

4. Sending the wrong invitation to a guest. Check names, guest allocations and event details before forwarding an invitation.

5. Making the message too long. Keep the accompanying text short. Put the additional information on the invitation card or wedding website.

6. Forgetting the RSVP deadline. If you need attendance confirmation, tell guests when and how to respond.

7. Sending an invitation to a group where not everyone is invited. This can create unnecessary embarrassment and misunderstandings.

8. Sharing private information publicly. Avoid posting personal phone numbers, private addresses, access details or guest-specific invitation links on public social media pages.

9. Sending an untested link. Open the invitation link yourself before sharing it with guests.

10. Using the wrong tone. A message to a close friend can be informal, while one to an elder or professional contact may require a more respectful approach.

Should You Send a Wedding Invitation Card or a Digital Invitation on WhatsApp?

Both printed and digital wedding invitations can serve important purposes.

Printed invitations may be preferred by some families, particularly when inviting older relatives, respected community members or guests who expect a physical invitation.

Digital invitations are convenient when you need to share information quickly with people in different locations. They can also make it easier to distribute updates and share links to additional event information.

For many Nigerian couples, using both formats can be a practical approach.

You could:

  • Print selected invitation cards for relatives and guests who prefer physical invitations.
  • Send digital invitations to friends, colleagues and guests living outside your city.
  • Share a wedding website for additional information.
  • Provide an RSVP link when you need to confirm attendance.

The best choice depends on your budget, guest list, family expectations and the type of wedding you are organising.

How AriyaHQ Can Help You Organise Your Wedding Invitations

Sending the right WhatsApp message is important, but organising the entire invitation process involves more than writing a few lines.

You also need to keep track of who has received an invitation, where guests can find the event information and whether people have confirmed attendance.

AriyaHQ is designed around event planning and digital event experiences. Couples exploring digital invitation and RSVP options can visit AriyaHQ to learn about the available tools for creating and managing their event experience.

Instead of relying entirely on scattered messages and manually maintained lists, consider using a more organised process for sharing event information and coordinating responses.

Explore AriyaHQ's digital invitation options and event RSVP options to see which services are available for your event.

Frequently Asked Questions About Wedding Invitation Messages on WhatsApp

1. How do I write a wedding invitation message on WhatsApp?

Start with a greeting, mention the names of the couple, state the wedding date and location, and explain that you would like the recipient to attend. Attach the invitation card or share the relevant link. If you need guests to confirm attendance, include an RSVP deadline and instructions.

2. What is a short wedding invitation message for WhatsApp?

You can write:

"Hello [Name], we are delighted to invite you to the wedding of [Bride's Name] and [Groom's Name] on [Date] at [Venue]. We would love to celebrate this special day with you. Please find our invitation attached. We hope to see you there!"

3. How do I invite someone to my wedding formally on WhatsApp?

Use a respectful greeting, identify the couple, provide the wedding date and venue, and express that you would be honoured by their presence. Avoid overly casual language when inviting senior relatives, professional contacts or family friends.

4. Can I send a wedding invitation through WhatsApp instead of printing cards?

Yes. Digital invitations can be shared through WhatsApp, making them useful for guests who live far away or prefer receiving event information online. However, some families and guests may still prefer printed invitations, so consider the expectations of your intended guests.

5. Should I send a wedding invitation message individually or in a group?

Individual messages are generally more suitable when the invitation is personal or when guests have different allocations. A group message can work when every member of the group is invited. Be careful not to create confusion by sending invitations to people who are not included in the guest list.

6. How do I ask guests to confirm attendance?

Add a polite RSVP request to your message. For example:

"Kindly confirm your attendance by [Date] using the link below so we can finalise our arrangements. Thank you."

Provide a working response link or a contact number that someone will monitor.

7. How early should I send wedding invitations on WhatsApp?

The right timing depends on the wedding date, guest locations and the amount of preparation guests may need. Give guests enough notice to arrange transport, accommodation and time away from work. Guests travelling from outside Nigeria or from distant states may need considerably more advance notice.

8. Can I send a wedding invitation to someone who lives abroad?

Yes. WhatsApp is useful for sharing invitations with guests living abroad. Include the city, full date, time zone where necessary and any travel or accommodation information that may help them plan.

9. What should I write when sending a wedding invitation card as an attachment?

You can write:

"Dear [Name], please find attached our wedding invitation. We would be delighted to have you join us as we celebrate on [Date] at [Venue]. We look forward to sharing this special day with you."

10. How do I remind guests about my wedding after sending the invitation?

Send a brief and polite reminder that references the original invitation. If you need an attendance confirmation, include the RSVP deadline and response method again.

Final Thoughts

A wedding invitation message does not have to be complicated. What matters is that it communicates the important details, reflects your relationship with the recipient and makes the person feel genuinely welcome.

Whether you are sending a formal invitation to an elderly relative, sharing your wedding plans with colleagues or inviting close friends, choose wording that feels natural and appropriate.

Most importantly, check the names, dates, venue details and invitation links before sending. A thoughtful message, supported by a well-organised invitation, can make the process easier for both you and your guests.

title: 30 Wedding Gift Ideas for Nigerian Couples: Thoughtful Gifts for Every Budget
excerpt: Looking for wedding gift ideas for Nigerian couples? Discover 30 thoughtful gifts, from home appliances to cash contributions and memorable experiences.
author: Ariya Journal
imageAlt: Black bride and groom sharing a wedding kiss in black and white
content:
Introduction

A Nigerian wedding is more than a ceremony. It is a celebration that brings together families, friends, colleagues and communities to witness the beginning of a new chapter in a couple's life.

After receiving an invitation, one question many guests begin to consider is: What should I give the couple as a wedding gift?

Some people prefer giving cash. Others would rather purchase something useful for the couple's home, contribute towards a major purchase or choose a personalised gift that the newlyweds can keep for years.

The challenge is finding something thoughtful, useful and appropriate for the couple.

A gift that looks impressive may not necessarily be what the couple needs. They may already own several kitchen appliances, have limited storage space or prefer to choose their own household items.

Whether you are attending a traditional wedding, white wedding or a combined celebration, this guide explores 30 wedding gift ideas for Nigerian couples, including practical household items, personalised presents, cash contributions and experiences.

What Makes a Good Wedding Gift for a Nigerian Couple?

Before choosing a gift, think about the couple's circumstances rather than simply buying something because it is commonly given at weddings.

A thoughtful wedding gift should ideally meet one or more of these considerations.

1. It should be useful

Many couples are preparing to establish or improve their homes after getting married. Household essentials, appliances, furniture and other practical items can make a meaningful difference.

2. It should suit the couple's lifestyle

Consider whether the couple lives in Nigeria or abroad, whether they are moving into a new home and what they enjoy doing together.

A gift that is useful to one couple may not be suitable for another.

3. It should fit your budget

You do not need to spend beyond your means to give a thoughtful wedding present. A modest but carefully selected gift can be just as meaningful as an expensive one.

4. It should not duplicate something they already own

If the couple has created a wedding wishlist or gift registry, check it before making a purchase.

This helps reduce duplicate gifts and gives you a better idea of what they actually need.

5. It should be easy to deliver

Consider how the gift will reach the couple. Large appliances, furniture and fragile items may be difficult to transport to a wedding reception.

You may need to arrange delivery to their home instead.

30 Wedding Gift Ideas for Nigerian Couples

The following suggestions cover different budgets, lifestyles and preferences. They are ideas rather than a prescribed list; choose what makes sense for the couple.

A. Practical Household and Kitchen Gifts

These are useful options for couples furnishing a home or replacing everyday household essentials.

1. A quality blender

A blender is useful for preparing smoothies, sauces, soups and other everyday meals. It can be a practical gift for couples who enjoy cooking at home.

Consider the motor power, jar capacity, durability and availability of replacement parts before buying.

2. A cookware or pot set

A quality cookware set can be a valuable addition to a newly established kitchen.

Look for durable materials, suitable pot sizes and handles that are comfortable to use. Stainless steel and other good-quality cookware options may be worth considering.

3. A dinner set

A dinner set is suitable for couples who enjoy hosting family and friends.

Choose a design that is versatile enough for everyday meals as well as special occasions.

4. An air fryer

An air fryer can be useful for couples who want another convenient way to prepare meals.

Before buying one, consider the available kitchen space, capacity, power requirements and warranty.

5. An electric kettle

An electric kettle is a simple household essential that many couples can use regularly.

It is also a suitable option when you want to give something practical without purchasing a large appliance.

6. A microwave oven

A microwave can make reheating food and preparing certain meals more convenient.

Check the kitchen's available space, the appliance's capacity and the couple's power arrangements before purchasing one.

7. A food processor or stand mixer

For couples who enjoy cooking or baking, a food processor or stand mixer can be a thoughtful gift.

These appliances can help with food preparation, mixing, chopping and other kitchen tasks.

8. Kitchen utensils and accessories

A carefully selected kitchen bundle could include:

  • Chopping boards
  • Quality knives
  • Measuring cups and spoons
  • Mixing bowls
  • Food storage containers
  • Serving spoons
  • Kitchen organisers

You can package several complementary items together to create a useful kitchen starter set.

B. Bedroom and Home Essentials

A couple's home requires more than kitchen equipment. Bedroom accessories, storage items and household essentials can also make thoughtful presents.

9. Quality bedsheets and bedding

A good bedsheet set can be a practical and elegant gift.

Consider the mattress size, material, colour preferences and number of pieces before purchasing.

10. A duvet and pillow set

A comfortable duvet and pillow set can help the couple furnish their bedroom.

Choose materials that are suitable for the climate and easy to maintain.

11. Curtains and window accessories

Curtains can improve privacy, manage sunlight and complement a room's interior design.

However, confirm the window measurements and preferred colours before buying.

12. Towels and bathroom essentials

A quality towel set is a useful gift that can include bath towels, hand towels and face towels.

You can also combine it with a matching bathroom accessory set.

13. A wardrobe or storage organiser

Storage solutions can help newlyweds organise clothes, shoes, accessories and household belongings.

If you are considering a large storage item, check the couple's available space first.

14. A decorative home accessory

A carefully selected decorative item can make a home feel more personal.

Ideas include:

  • A tasteful wall clock
  • A decorative mirror
  • A simple vase
  • A framed artwork
  • A stylish table lamp

Avoid very specific decorative pieces unless you understand the couple's taste.

C. Electronics and Home Convenience Gifts

For couples who appreciate technology and household convenience, electronics can be useful wedding presents.

15. A television

A television can be a substantial gift for a couple setting up a new home.

Consider screen size, available space, connectivity, warranty and the couple's entertainment preferences.

16. A rechargeable fan

Power arrangements are an important consideration for many Nigerian households.

A rechargeable fan may provide additional convenience during periods when electricity is unavailable.

Check battery capacity, runtime, replacement options and product warranty.

17. A washing machine

A washing machine can be a significant household gift that helps reduce the time and effort spent on laundry.

Consider the machine's capacity, water requirements, installation needs and available space.

18. A home power solution

Depending on the budget, a home power gift could include a rechargeable lamp, a suitable backup power device or a contribution towards an inverter or solar installation.

For larger systems, consult the couple before purchasing because their power needs and existing electrical setup matter.

19. A wireless speaker

A wireless speaker can be suitable for couples who enjoy music, entertainment and hosting friends.

Choose a model with good sound quality, reliable connectivity and a warranty.

D. Personalised and Sentimental Wedding Gifts

Not every wedding gift needs to be a household appliance. Some of the most memorable presents are those that celebrate the couple's relationship.

20. A personalised photo frame

A photo frame featuring the couple's names or wedding date can serve as a lasting reminder of their special day.

You could also leave space for them to insert their favourite wedding photograph.

21. A customised photo album

A personalised photo album gives the couple a place to preserve photographs from their wedding, honeymoon and future milestones.

22. A customised couple portrait

A commissioned illustration or portrait can make a thoughtful keepsake.

If you choose this option, use a suitable photograph and allow enough time for the artist to complete the work.

23. Engraved glassware

Personalised wine glasses, drinking glasses or other suitable glassware can make an elegant present.

Confirm the couple's preferences before selecting the type of glassware.

24. A personalised memory box

A memory box can hold photographs, letters, wedding souvenirs and other keepsakes.

It is particularly suitable for couples who enjoy preserving memories.

E. Cash Gifts and Shared Contributions

Cash gifts are a flexible option because the couple can decide how best to use the contribution.

They may put it towards household expenses, furniture, travel, accommodation or another priority.

25. A cash gift in an envelope

A cash gift in a clearly labelled envelope is a straightforward option.

Include your name and a short congratulatory message so the couple can identify and appreciate your gift.

Give an amount that is comfortable for you. There is no universal amount every wedding guest is expected to give.

26. A honeymoon contribution

You can contribute towards the couple's honeymoon, whether it is a local getaway or an international trip.

If you know their travel plans, you may choose to support accommodation, transport or an activity they would enjoy.

27. A contribution towards their new home

Setting up a home can involve several expenses, including furniture, appliances, household supplies and other essentials.

A contribution towards one of these needs can be particularly useful.

28. A group gift from friends or colleagues

If you and several other guests want to purchase a more substantial item, consider pooling your contributions.

For example, a group could contribute towards:

  • A refrigerator
  • A washing machine
  • A television
  • A dining set
  • A home power solution
  • A furniture purchase

Agree on the item, contribution amounts and delivery arrangements before collecting money.

F. Experiences and Services

Some couples may already have most of the household items they need. In that situation, an experience or service may be more appropriate.

29. A couples' experience

Consider gifting an experience they can enjoy together, such as:

  • A dinner at a restaurant
  • A weekend hotel stay
  • A spa experience
  • A cooking class
  • A short local getaway
  • Tickets to an event they would enjoy

Make sure the voucher or booking has flexible dates where possible.

30. A home service or professional service

A service can be just as useful as a physical present.

Depending on the couple's preferences, you could arrange:

  • A professional home cleaning session
  • An interior design consultation
  • A photography session
  • A home organisation service
  • A meal delivery package

Confirm that the couple would welcome the service before making a booking.

Wedding Gift Ideas Based on Your Budget

Your gift should reflect what you can comfortably afford. It is not necessary to compete with other guests or stretch your finances because you are attending a wedding.

Here is a simple way to organise your choices:

  • Small, thoughtful gift: an electric kettle, glasses, kitchen utensils or a personalised frame.
  • Practical household gift: bedsheets, a dinner set, towels, cookware or kitchen accessories.
  • Mid-range appliance: a blender, air fryer, rechargeable fan or wireless speaker.
  • Larger individual gift: a microwave, television, washing machine or other substantial home item.
  • Group contribution: a refrigerator, furniture, home power solution or honeymoon contribution.
  • Non-material gift: a dinner experience, hotel stay or professional home service.

These are categories rather than current Nigerian market price bands. Actual prices vary by brand, specification, seller and location.

Cash Gift or Physical Wedding Gift: Which Is Better?

There is no single answer. Both options can be appropriate, depending on what the couple wants and what you can comfortably provide.

When cash may be the better option

Cash gives the couple flexibility. They can use it towards whatever they need most, particularly if they are still furnishing their home or managing post-wedding expenses.

It can also be more convenient for guests travelling from another country or city.

When a physical gift may be better

A physical present may be suitable when:

  • You know exactly what the couple needs.
  • The item appears on their wishlist.
  • You want to give something they can use regularly.
  • You have found something personal and meaningful.
  • You know how and where it will be delivered.

Consider combining both

If you want to give a physical gift but also provide some financial support, you can combine a smaller household item with a cash contribution.

Ultimately, the couple's preferences should guide your decision.

Wedding Gift Etiquette: 8 Things Every Guest Should Know

Giving a wedding present is a thoughtful gesture, but there are a few things to consider before making your choice.

1. Check whether the couple has a gift registry

A wedding gift registry or wishlist can help you identify items the couple actually wants or needs.

Check the list before purchasing anything.

2. Do not feel pressured to overspend

Your relationship with the couple, your personal circumstances and your budget are all relevant.

A wedding gift should not put you under financial pressure.

3. Avoid buying duplicate household items

If you are purchasing an appliance or home accessory, check whether the couple already owns it or whether another guest has selected it.

4. Include your name and a message

A gift card helps the couple identify who gave the present.

A simple message such as "Congratulations on your wedding. Wishing you a lifetime of happiness" is enough.

5. Arrange delivery for large gifts

Large appliances and furniture may be inconvenient to transport from a wedding reception.

Where possible, arrange delivery to the couple's home at an agreed time.

6. Respect the couple's stated preferences

If the couple has requested cash gifts, a particular type of present or contributions through a specified arrangement, respect their preference.

7. Consider guests travelling from abroad

Shipping a physical gift internationally may involve customs, delivery costs and delays.

A monetary contribution or a gift purchased locally may be more practical.

8. Give thoughtfully, not competitively

Do not choose a gift simply because you want it to look more expensive than what other guests are giving.

The intention behind the gift matters more than its price.

How Couples Can Make Wedding Gifting Easier for Their Guests

If you are planning your wedding, you can make the gifting experience easier by giving guests some guidance.

Many guests genuinely want to purchase something useful but do not know what the couple needs.

Consider these steps:

Create a list of things you actually need

Think about your home, lifestyle and future plans.

Your list might include kitchen appliances, bedding, furniture, household accessories or contributions towards specific goals.

Include different options

Not every guest has the same budget.

A thoughtful wishlist should include a range of options so guests can choose something suitable for their circumstances.

Avoid adding things you do not need

A wishlist should help guests make decisions, not become a list of expensive items you would like to own.

Prioritise useful and meaningful choices.

Share the list clearly

If you have a wedding website or a gift registry, include the relevant link in your invitation or share it with guests through an appropriate channel.

Make sure the instructions are easy to understand.

Keep the list updated

If an item has already been selected or purchased, update the list where your chosen platform supports it. This can help reduce duplicate purchases.

How AriyaHQ Fits into the Wedding Wishlist Experience

Choosing a wedding gift should be straightforward for guests, and couples should be able to communicate their preferences clearly.

A wedding wishlist or gift registry can help bridge that gap by giving couples a place to organise the gifts they would appreciate and giving guests a clearer idea of what to choose.

If you are planning your wedding, explore AriyaHQ's wedding wishlist and gift registry pages to learn about the available options.

Check the current product details before relying on any particular contribution, payment or gift-fulfilment functionality.

Frequently Asked Questions About Wedding Gift Ideas for Nigerian Couples

1. What is the best wedding gift for a Nigerian couple?

The best gift depends on the couple's needs and preferences. Practical household items, cash contributions, kitchen appliances, quality bedding and personalised keepsakes are all possible choices. If the couple has a wishlist, use it as your starting point.

2. What can I buy as a wedding gift in Nigeria?

You can consider a blender, cookware set, dinner set, air fryer, bedsheets, towels, microwave, rechargeable fan, personalised photo frame or another useful household item. Choose something that suits the couple's lifestyle and your budget.

3. Is cash an acceptable wedding gift in Nigeria?

Yes. Cash is a flexible wedding gift that allows couples to decide how best to use the money. You can place it in a named envelope or use another method specified by the couple.

4. What is a good affordable wedding gift?

An electric kettle, quality bedsheets, kitchen utensils, a set of glasses, a dinner set or a personalised photo frame can make thoughtful gifts. The most important thing is choosing something appropriate rather than spending more than you can afford.

5. What should I buy for a couple who already has everything?

Consider an experience, a personalised keepsake, a contribution towards their honeymoon or a service they would appreciate. You could also ask a close family member whether the couple has any outstanding needs.

6. Should I buy a wedding gift if I am already contributing to Aso-Ebi?

That depends on your circumstances and the couple's expectations. Buying Aso-Ebi does not automatically mean you must purchase an additional gift. If you would like to give something, choose an amount or item that fits your budget.

7. Is it better to give cash or a household item?

Both are acceptable options. Cash provides flexibility, while a household item can be useful when you know what the couple needs. A wedding wishlist can help you decide.

8. What is a wedding gift registry?

A wedding gift registry is a list or organised collection of gifts that a couple would like to receive. It helps guests choose presents based on the couple's preferences and can reduce duplicate or unwanted gifts.

9. Can friends contribute towards one wedding gift?

Yes. Friends, colleagues, relatives or members of a group can combine their contributions to purchase a larger item or fund a shared experience. Agree on the arrangements before collecting contributions.

10. What should I avoid buying as a wedding gift?

Avoid items that are excessively personal, difficult to transport, unsuitable for the couple's lifestyle or likely to be duplicated. Also avoid purchasing expensive appliances without considering the couple's available space and preferences.

Final Thoughts

A wedding gift is a way of celebrating a couple and showing support as they begin a new chapter together.

It could be a useful kitchen appliance, a set of quality bedsheets, a personalised keepsake, a contribution towards their honeymoon or simply cash that helps them meet an important need.

The best wedding gift is not necessarily the most expensive. It is one chosen with the couple in mind.

If you are attending a wedding, consider the couple's preferences before making a purchase. And if you are getting married, creating a thoughtful wishlist can make it easier for your guests to choose gifts you will genuinely appreciate.

Planning your wedding? Explore AriyaHQ's wedding planning and gifting resources to discover ways to organise your celebration and communicate your preferences to guests.

title: What to Put on a Wedding Wishlist: A Practical Checklist for Nigerian Couples
excerpt: Not sure what to add to your wedding wishlist? Explore practical gift ideas, household essentials and experiences Nigerian couples can include in their list.
author: Ariya Journal
imageAlt: Nigerian bride and groom in traditional coral bead wedding attire
content:
Introduction

Planning a wedding involves making decisions about the ceremony, reception, guests, outfits, vendors and countless other details. But beyond the celebration itself, there is another important part of preparing for married life: deciding what you and your partner need as you begin your journey together.

This is where a wedding wishlist becomes useful.

A wedding wishlist gives you a way to communicate the gifts that would genuinely be helpful to you as a couple. Instead of receiving several versions of the same kitchen appliance or decorative item you may never use, your guests have a better idea of what you need.

However, deciding what belongs on your list can be surprisingly difficult.

Should you include kitchen appliances? What about bedding, electronics, furniture or contributions towards an experience? Should you add expensive items alongside affordable ones? And how do you create a list that reflects your lifestyle without making guests feel pressured?

This guide answers those questions and provides a practical wedding wishlist checklist for Nigerian couples.

What Is a Wedding Wishlist?

A wedding wishlist is a list of gifts a couple would appreciate receiving from their wedding guests.

It can contain household essentials, kitchen equipment, electronics, bedroom accessories, furniture, personalised gifts and other items that would be useful to the couple.

Some couples create a list because they are setting up a new home. Others already have most of their household essentials but would appreciate upgrades, experiences or items that support their lifestyle.

A wedding wishlist is not an instruction that guests must buy something. It is simply a guide for people who would like to give a gift but are unsure what to choose.

Why Should You Create a Wedding Wishlist?

Creating a wishlist is not about asking people for expensive presents. It is about making gift-giving more thoughtful and helping you avoid unnecessary duplicates.

Here are some reasons to consider creating one.

1. It helps you receive gifts you actually need

You and your partner may already know the things you need for your home. Your guests, however, may not know whether you need a blender, a microwave, a set of bedsheets or another dinner set.

A wishlist gives them useful direction.

2. It reduces duplicate gifts

Imagine receiving three blenders, two kettles and four sets of dinner plates after your wedding.

Although the gifts may be appreciated, duplicates can create storage problems and may require you to exchange or give away items.

A properly organised list can help reduce this possibility, especially when the platform or process you use allows guests to see which gifts have already been selected.

3. It helps you plan your new home

If you are moving into a new apartment after your wedding, your wishlist can help you identify the essentials you still need.

You can organise the list by room and prioritise the items that will make the biggest difference to your everyday life.

4. It gives guests options at different budgets

Not every guest will have the same financial capacity.

A thoughtful wishlist should include a mixture of affordable, moderately priced and more substantial gift ideas. This allows guests to choose something that feels comfortable for them.

5. It encourages more personal gifts

Your wishlist does not have to contain only household equipment.

You can include books, personalised keepsakes, travel accessories, experiences and other gifts that reflect your interests as a couple.

What to Put on Your Wedding Wishlist: 10 Essential Categories

The best wedding wishlist is one that reflects how you and your partner intend to live.

You do not need to include every item in this guide. Use the categories below to identify what you genuinely need.

1. Kitchen Appliances

Kitchen appliances are among the most practical items couples can include on a wedding wishlist, particularly if they are setting up a new home.

Consider adding:

  • Blender
  • Food processor
  • Air fryer
  • Microwave
  • Electric kettle
  • Toaster
  • Rice cooker
  • Stand mixer
  • Hand mixer
  • Coffee maker
  • Sandwich maker
  • Juicer
  • Electric pressure cooker
  • Water dispenser

A Nigerian household consideration: Think about how you actually prepare meals. A blender, food processor or reliable cooking equipment may be more useful to your household than an appliance you are unlikely to use.

Also consider the appliance's power requirements, warranty, availability of replacement parts and suitability for your kitchen.

2. Cookware and Kitchen Utensils

Not every useful kitchen gift needs to be an electrical appliance.

You can add:

  • Non-stick cooking pots
  • Stainless steel pots
  • Frying pans
  • Sauce pans
  • Baking trays
  • Oven dishes
  • Chopping boards
  • Kitchen knives
  • Cooking spoons
  • Serving spoons
  • Mixing bowls
  • Measuring cups
  • Food storage containers
  • Spice racks
  • Dish racks
  • Kitchen organisers

If you already own basic cookware, consider requesting a durable upgrade rather than adding several similar sets.

3. Dinnerware and Dining Essentials

Dinnerware is useful for everyday meals, entertaining guests and hosting family members.

Consider including:

  • Dinner plate sets
  • Soup bowls
  • Serving bowls
  • Drinking glasses
  • Mugs
  • Cutlery sets
  • Serving trays
  • Water jugs
  • Table mats
  • Table runners
  • Food flasks
  • Serving dishes
  • Cake stands

Think about the number of people you typically entertain. A couple who regularly hosts family and friends may need more serving pieces than a couple who prefers smaller gatherings.

4. Bedroom Essentials

Your bedroom is one of the spaces where comfort and quality matter.

Useful wishlist additions include:

  • Bedsheets
  • Duvet sets
  • Pillows
  • Pillowcases
  • Mattress protectors
  • Blankets
  • Bedside lamps
  • Laundry baskets
  • Wardrobe organisers
  • Shoe organisers
  • Storage boxes
  • Dressing mirrors

Before adding bedding, confirm your mattress size. A beautiful bedsheet that does not fit your bed is not particularly useful.

5. Bathroom and Personal Care Essentials

Bathroom items are easy to overlook when preparing a new home, but they are part of everyday living.

You could include:

  • Bath towels
  • Hand towels
  • Bath mats
  • Shower curtains
  • Bathroom organisers
  • Soap dispensers
  • Laundry hampers
  • Bathroom mirrors
  • Hair dryers
  • Electric grooming appliances
  • Toiletry organisers

Choose colours and designs that fit the bathroom you intend to use.

6. Home Appliances and Electronics

If you are setting up a home together, larger appliances may be among your most valuable wishlist additions.

Consider:

  • Television
  • Refrigerator
  • Washing machine
  • Standing fan
  • Rechargeable fan
  • Air conditioner
  • Vacuum cleaner
  • Steam iron
  • Ironing board
  • Generator or inverter-related equipment
  • Solar power equipment
  • Extension sockets and surge protectors

In Nigeria, power reliability and electricity consumption are practical considerations when choosing appliances. Check the energy requirements, warranty, installation needs and available servicing options before adding expensive equipment.

For major appliances, make sure you have agreed on the size and specifications that will fit your home.

7. Furniture and Home Organisation

If you are furnishing a new apartment, furniture and storage solutions may be more useful than smaller decorative gifts.

Possible additions include:

  • Dining table and chairs
  • Centre table
  • Bedside tables
  • Bookshelves
  • Shoe racks
  • Storage cabinets
  • Wardrobe organisers
  • Laundry storage
  • Wall shelves
  • Study desk
  • Office chair
  • Shoe cabinet

Measure your available space before adding furniture to your wishlist. It is better to receive something that fits your home than an item you have to struggle to accommodate.

8. Home Décor and Personalised Gifts

Your wishlist should also reflect your taste as a couple.

You may include:

  • Framed photographs
  • Personalised wall art
  • Couple portraits
  • Decorative mirrors
  • Table lamps
  • Vases
  • Throw pillows
  • Rugs
  • Decorative trays
  • Photo albums
  • Engraved glassware
  • Personalised keepsake boxes

These gifts can make your home feel more personal, especially when they reflect shared memories or interests.

However, avoid adding too many decorative items if you have not settled on your preferred interior style.

9. Travel and Experience Gifts

Not every wedding gift has to be something you can place in your home.

If you and your partner enjoy travelling, exploring new places or trying new activities, consider adding:

  • Luggage sets
  • Carry-on bags
  • Travel organisers
  • Passport holders
  • Weekend getaway experiences
  • Dinner experiences
  • Couple photography sessions
  • Spa experiences
  • Cooking classes
  • Activity or experience vouchers

For travel-related gifts, be clear about the kind of experience you would appreciate. Check any expiry dates, restrictions and booking conditions before adding vouchers or packages.

10. Practical Services and Shared Gifts

Some couples may benefit more from a service or a larger shared gift than another physical item.

Depending on what is available and suitable, ideas include:

  • Professional home cleaning
  • Interior design consultation
  • Home organisation services
  • Furniture contributions
  • A group gift towards a major appliance
  • A photography session
  • A couple's experience

For shared gifts, explain what the gift is intended to support. Do not assume that a platform supports pooled payments or contributions unless you have confirmed that functionality.

Wedding Wishlist Checklist for Nigerian Couples

Use this checklist to review the items you may want to include. You can select only the categories that apply to your home and lifestyle.

Kitchen

  • Blender
  • Food processor
  • Air fryer
  • Microwave
  • Electric kettle
  • Toaster
  • Rice cooker
  • Cooking pots
  • Frying pans
  • Dinnerware
  • Cutlery
  • Drinking glasses
  • Food storage containers
  • Kitchen organisers

Bedroom

  • Bedsheets
  • Duvet
  • Pillows
  • Pillowcases
  • Mattress protector
  • Bedside lamps
  • Laundry basket
  • Wardrobe organisers

Bathroom

  • Bath towels
  • Hand towels
  • Bath mats
  • Bathroom organisers
  • Shower curtain
  • Laundry hamper

Living Room

  • Television
  • Standing fan
  • Rechargeable fan
  • Centre table
  • Rugs
  • Curtains
  • Decorative mirrors
  • Wall art
  • Throw pillows

Household Appliances

  • Refrigerator
  • Washing machine
  • Vacuum cleaner
  • Steam iron
  • Air conditioner
  • Power backup equipment

Personal and Experience Gifts

  • Luggage
  • Travel accessories
  • Personalised gifts
  • Couple photography
  • Dinner experience
  • Weekend getaway
  • Home service

How to Choose the Right Items for Your Wedding Wishlist

Having a long list of possible gifts does not mean you should add everything.

The goal is to create a list that is useful, realistic and considerate of your guests.

1. Start with what you already own

Before creating your wishlist, take an inventory of your current belongings.

Identify:

  • Items you already own and are happy with.
  • Items you own but would like to replace.
  • Items you do not have.
  • Items you may need in the next one to two years.

This prevents you from requesting unnecessary duplicates.

2. Discuss your priorities as a couple

Your wishlist should reflect the needs of both partners.

One person may prioritise kitchen appliances, while the other may prefer electronics, travel accessories or furniture.

Discuss your plans for your home and agree on the items that would be most useful.

3. Include different price levels

A good wishlist should not consist entirely of expensive appliances.

Include smaller items such as mugs, towels and kitchen utensils alongside larger items such as refrigerators, televisions and washing machines.

This gives guests more flexibility when choosing a gift.

4. Prioritise quality over quantity

It is better to receive a few durable and useful items than many products that may not last.

For appliances, check the manufacturer's warranty, servicing arrangements and availability of replacement parts.

For furniture and household items, consider durability, size and material.

5. Be specific about what you want

Avoid vague descriptions such as:

  • Blender
  • Television
  • Bedsheets
  • Cooking pots

Instead, provide useful details where possible:

  • Blender with a durable motor and suitable capacity.
  • Television with your preferred screen size and specifications.
  • Bedsheets in your mattress size.
  • Stainless steel cookware set with the pieces you need.

Specific descriptions reduce the chances of receiving something unsuitable.

6. Think about your living arrangements

If you will be moving into a new apartment, consider the available space, electrical requirements and existing fittings.

If you already live together, focus on upgrades and missing essentials rather than starting your list from scratch.

7. Review the list before sharing it

Check for duplicates, outdated preferences and items you no longer need.

Make sure the descriptions are clear and that the list is easy for guests to understand.

How Many Items Should a Wedding Wishlist Have?

There is no fixed number of items every couple must include.

The right number depends on your guest list, household needs, budget preferences and the range of gifts you would genuinely appreciate.

A useful starting point is to include enough options to give guests a choice without making the list unnecessarily long.

You can organise it into three broad groups:

  • Everyday essentials: towels, mugs, cookware and bedsheets.
  • Home upgrades: an air fryer, television, washing machine or furniture.
  • Personal gifts: luggage, personalised keepsakes and experiences.

The important thing is variety. Guests should be able to find an appropriate option without feeling that they must purchase a particular item.

Wedding Wishlist Mistakes to Avoid

Even a well-intentioned wishlist can become difficult to use if it is poorly organised.

Avoid these common mistakes.

Adding items you do not actually need

Do not include something simply because it is popular on another couple's registry. Your wishlist should reflect your own lifestyle.

Including only expensive gifts

A list dominated by high-value appliances can make guests feel uncomfortable. Add smaller, practical options too.

Forgetting the dimensions and specifications

Furniture, appliances and bedding should have clear sizes and specifications.

Adding too many decorative items

Personalised gifts and home décor are lovely, but practical household needs should not be overlooked if you are setting up a new home.

Not considering cultural and family expectations

Nigerian weddings often involve different family customs and gift-giving expectations. A wedding wishlist is separate from traditional marriage requirements, such as the items requested by a bride's family. Do not confuse a couple's optional gift wishlist with a traditional engagement or marriage list.

Failing to communicate the wishlist politely

Guests should understand that the list is a guide, not a requirement. Make it clear that their presence and support are appreciated regardless of whether they bring a gift.

How to Share Your Wedding Wishlist with Guests

Once your wishlist is ready, think about how you will make it available to people who ask what you would like as a wedding gift.

You can share it through:

  • Your wedding website.
  • A message sent privately to guests who ask about gifts.
  • A digital wedding invitation, where appropriate.
  • A family representative or member of the wedding party.

Avoid making the wishlist the main focus of your invitation. The invitation should primarily communicate the celebration details.

You can use a polite message such as:

Example wedding wishlist message

"Your presence at our wedding means so much to us, and we are grateful to have you celebrate this special moment with us. For those who have asked about gifts, we have put together a wishlist of a few things we would appreciate as we begin this new chapter. Please know that there is absolutely no obligation. Your love, prayers and support mean more to us than anything."

You can adapt this message to your preferred tone and share the wishlist link when appropriate.

How Ariya Can Help You Organise Your Wedding Wishlist

Once you have decided what you and your partner need, the next step is making the list easy to organise and share.

Ariya provides wedding and event-planning tools intended to help couples coordinate important parts of their celebrations. If you are preparing a wedding wishlist, explore the available wishlist and registry options on Ariya to see how they can support the way you want to present your gift preferences to guests.

You can also explore Ariya's wedding planning resources and digital invitation options as you organise the other details of your celebration.

Ready to organise your wedding gift list? Explore Ariya's wedding wishlist page and see how it fits into your wedding planning process.

Frequently Asked Questions About Wedding Wishlists

What should I put on my wedding wishlist?

You can include kitchen appliances, cookware, dinnerware, bedding, bathroom essentials, electronics, furniture, home décor, travel accessories and experiences. Choose items that reflect your actual needs and lifestyle as a couple.

Should a wedding wishlist contain only household items?

No. A wedding wishlist can include household essentials, personalised gifts, travel accessories, experiences and other things you and your partner would appreciate.

How much should items on a wedding wishlist cost?

There is no universal price requirement. Include a range of options so guests can choose gifts that suit their individual budgets. Avoid making guests feel that they must spend a particular amount.

Is a wedding wishlist the same as a traditional marriage list in Nigeria?

No. A wedding wishlist is a voluntary list of gifts a couple would appreciate receiving. A traditional marriage list is based on the customs and requirements of the families involved and may include specific items requested for the marriage ceremony.

Should couples include cash gifts on their wedding wishlist?

That depends on the couple's preference and the arrangements available through the platform they use. If you would appreciate monetary gifts, communicate this politely and confirm how any contributions can be made. Do not assume that every registry platform supports cash contributions.

When should we create our wedding wishlist?

It is helpful to start once you have a clearer idea of your living arrangements and household needs. Creating it early gives you time to review the list, remove unnecessary items and share it when guests begin asking about gifts.

How do we avoid receiving duplicate wedding gifts?

Use an organised wishlist or registry that clearly communicates the items you want. Where the platform supports it, look for a feature that allows guests to mark selected gifts as purchased or reserved. You can also coordinate with a trusted family member or wedding representative.

Is it rude to share a wedding wishlist with guests?

Not necessarily. The way you communicate it matters. Share it politely, preferably when guests ask about gifts, and make it clear that there is no obligation to purchase anything.

Final Thoughts

A wedding wishlist should make the gift-giving experience easier for everyone.

For couples, it provides an opportunity to identify the things that will genuinely support their life together. For guests, it offers inspiration and helps them choose gifts with greater confidence.

You do not need to fill your list with every appliance, piece of furniture or decorative item you can find. Start with your needs, discuss your priorities as a couple and include a variety of options.

The most meaningful wedding gifts are not necessarily the most expensive. They are the ones chosen with thought, care and an understanding of the life the couple is building together.
